claims.text: Alloying a high-entropy alloy with elements having significantly different atomic radii introduces lattice distortions.
Phonon scattering caused by lattice distortions reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
The modified alloy will have lower phonon thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable untreated alloy.
The hypothesis applies to high-entropy alloys in either an as-cast or solution-treated state.
The predicted reduction applies from 300 K to 1000 K at 1 atm.
The comparator is an untreated high-entropy alloy of the same composition but without the alloying elements.

contradictions.description: Adding alloying elements necessarily changes composition, so a baseline described as both 'of the same composition' and 'without the alloying elements' cannot generally exist. The intended control would need either compositional substitution at fixed total atomic fraction or a clearly specified unmodified reference composition.
